doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Little mixing of black and white musicians; playing West Memphis, Arkansas
summary: Almost no integration, though they played white-owned clubs across the bridge in West Memphis for white audiences.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: That’s interesting. So was there any mixing between the white and the black musicians at this time?

Very, very little. Yes. I really can’t call it integrated, no, ‘cause like I said because it was before the total segregation. But what we would do, we could go to places like West Memphis, Arkansas, which was like across the bridge from us, and we would play in the white-owned club for the white audience, but it was totally segregated.
